questions.topic: Practice-setting reference resources and manager approval

choices.why: Incorrect. Insurance coverage information does not substitute for the required interchangeability resource.

choices.text: Current laws and regulations governing pharmacy practice.

choices.text: A current veterinary drug handbook or another Board-approved veterinary reference.
choices.why: Correct. The rule expressly includes a veterinary reference.

questions.topic: New prescription pickup during sole-pharmacist break

questions.critical_exception: Prior preparation, visual check and pharmacist DUR are stipulated; other security, premises and break conditions remain applicable.

A patient arrives for a new prescription already prepared, visually checked and subjected to pharmacist drug utilization review. Which measures are required under the temporary-absence rule? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Obtain the prescriber's confirmation of the completed prescription.
choices.why: Incorrect. Additional prescriber confirmation is not required by the break exception.

choices.text: Keep a transaction log that includes the patient's telephone number.

questions.topic: Prescription pads bearing pharmacy identification

choices.why: Incorrect. A disclaimer does not remove the prohibition on providing forms referring to a pharmacy.

choices.text: Supply the named pads if they are used for noncontrolled prescriptions.
choices.why: Incorrect. The prohibition is not limited to controlled-substance prescriptions.

choices.text: Supply the named pads for payment rather than as a gift.
choices.why: Incorrect. Charging for the pads does not change the restriction.

questions.topic: Continuing education across graduation and first full year

questions.topic: Reporting final discipline in another profession versus pending charge

choices.why: Incorrect. The final action on another health-care credential is subject to the seven-business-day provision.

choices.text: Report the pending charge within seven business days.
choices.why: Incorrect. Pending criminal charges are governed by the separate 30-day written-reporting provision.

choices.why: Correct. The rule reaches other health-care credentials and actions in other jurisdictions.

choices.why: Correct. The criminal reporting provision requires a written report within 30 days.

questions.topic: Prescriber agent preparation versus signature responsibility
questions.trigger: An otherwise lawful paper prescription for a federally controlled medication is permitted in the circumstances. A prescriber's secretary types the drug, quantity and patient details. Who may sign the prescription as the issuing practitioner?
questions.legal_decision: Separate delegated preparation from practitioner issuance and signature.
questions.critical_exception: Paper issuance is stipulated to be permitted; all other applicable form requirements remain.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the issuing practitioner signs the appropriately prepared paper prescription, agent preparation alone is not a defect.
questions.stem: An otherwise lawful paper prescription for a federally controlled medication is permitted in the circumstances. A prescriber's secretary types the drug, quantity and patient details. Who may sign the prescription as the issuing practitioner?

choices.text: The prescribing practitioner, who remains responsible for its compliance.
choices.why: Correct. An agent may prepare the prescription, but practitioner signature and responsibility remain required.

choices.text: The secretary, if the practitioner subsequently reviews the prescription.
choices.why: Incorrect. Subsequent review cannot substitute for the required practitioner signature.

choices.text: The secretary, using the practitioner's signature stamp with permission.
choices.why: Incorrect. An agent's stamp is not the required manual practitioner signature.

choices.text: A pharmacist, after confirming the intended order with the secretary.
choices.why: Incorrect. The pharmacist cannot supply the practitioner's signature.

choices.text: Another practitioner who witnesses preparation but does not issue the order.
choices.why: Incorrect. Witnessing preparation does not make that practitioner the issuer.

critical_error_options.reason: Treats an agent signature as practitioner signature.
Treats delegated stamping as required manual signature.

questions.topic: Medical need notation for GHB

choices.why: Incorrect. Specialty certification is not the specified notation.

choices.text: The patient's prior controlled-substance refill dates.
choices.why: Incorrect. Refill dates are not the required special entry.

choices.text: The patient's medical need for the prescription.

questions.topic: Missing versus incorrect patient address on Schedule II order

questions.legal_decision: Distinguish addition of an omitted address from changing an existing one.

questions.stem: An otherwise valid, permitted new paper Schedule II prescription omits the patient's address. The pharmacist independently verifies it. Which action completes the required address information without contacting the prescriber?

choices.text: Process the prescription without adding the address.
choices.why: Incorrect. The address is required information; the permitted addition resolves the omission.

questions.topic: Hospital narcotic maintenance incidental to unrelated inpatient treatment
questions.trigger: A patient receiving methadone maintenance is admitted to a hospital for fracture surgery. The hospital is not separately registered as an opioid treatment program. Assume all other applicable authorization and hospital-order requirements are met. Which statements reflect the federal inpatient exception?

questions.counterfactual_flip: If treatment is an ordinary outpatient methadone maintenance program, the incidental hospital exception does not authorize it.

Assume all other applicable authorization and hospital-order requirements are met. Which statements reflect the federal inpatient exception? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Authorized hospital staff may administer or dispense the narcotic as an incidental adjunct to treatment of the fracture.

choices.why: Incorrect. That limit belongs to the separate emergency dispensing provision, not the incidental inpatient provision.

choices.why: Correct. The provision does not impose the ordinary maintenance or detoxification limits on this described hospital treatment.

choices.text: The hospital exception does not itself authorize an outpatient methadone maintenance prescription at discharge.
choices.why: Correct. It is a provision for administration or dispensing in the hospital and is not independent outpatient prescribing authority.

choices.text: The same hospital exception permits the physician to operate a general outpatient methadone maintenance practice.
choices.why: Incorrect. The exception is limited to the specified inpatient circumstances; an outpatient program requires its own lawful basis.

questions.topic: Repeated therapy and offer to counsel

choices.why: Incorrect. Actual counseling is required for new and significant therapies; the offer is broader.

choices.why: Incorrect. A prior counseling encounter does not establish a current refusal.

choices.text: Patient's insurance member number.
choices.why: Incorrect. The cell-specific rule does not list insurance identifiers.

choices.text: Strength of each drug in the cell.
choices.why: Correct. The specific rule requires drug strengths.

choices.text: Wholesale supplier's account number.
choices.why: Incorrect. Supplier account numbers are not required on individual cells.

questions.topic: Compliance-package capacity and dosage-form damage
questions.trigger: A pharmacy prepares multi-drug single-dose pouches. Seven scheduled tablets are otherwise compatible, but their combined size exceeds the pouch capacity and risks crushing individual dosage forms. Other requirements are met. What should the pharmacist do?
questions.legal_decision: Redesign the package to meet capacity and integrity requirements.
questions.critical_exception: A suitable package must also satisfy compatibility, USP, labeling and applicable drug-schedule requirements.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the package is of sufficient capacity and does not risk damaging the dosage forms, this specific barrier is removed.
questions.stem: A pharmacy prepares multi-drug single-dose pouches. Seven scheduled tablets are otherwise compatible, but their combined size exceeds the pouch capacity and risks crushing individual dosage forms. Other requirements are met. What should the pharmacist do?

choices.text: Use the original pouch and shorten the assigned expiration date.
choices.why: Incorrect. A shorter date does not resolve a physical capacity or damage problem.

choices.text: Use the original pouch if the seal passes a leak test.
choices.why: Incorrect. A sound seal does not cure overloading or the risk of dosage-form damage.

choices.text: Use suitable larger or separate compliant packages that avoid overloading and damage.
choices.why: Correct. The rule prohibits exceeding container capacity or risking damage to individual dosage forms.

choices.text: Keep the original pouch design after obtaining the patient's consent.
choices.why: Incorrect. Patient consent does not waive the packaging standard.

choices.text: Retain the original pouch if the pharmacist documents a final visual inspection.
choices.why: Incorrect. Inspection does not authorize a known noncompliant package design.

critical_error_options.reason: Treats patient consent as a waiver of a known package-integrity requirement.

questions.topic: Pseudoephedrine seller training covers cashier
questions.trigger: A pharmacy sells pseudoephedrine at a restricted counter. One employee hands the product to customers, and another directly accepts payment. Which federal seller-training obligations apply?
questions.legal_decision: Identify covered sales roles and associated documentation.
questions.critical_exception: Placement, purchaser identification and sales-log requirements apply separately.
questions.counterfactual_flip: An employee with neither covered sales role is not covered by this particular description merely by working in the store.
questions.stem: A pharmacy sells pseudoephedrine at a restricted counter. One employee hands the product to customers, and another directly accepts payment. Which federal seller-training obligations apply? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Train the employee handing the product to purchasers.
choices.why: Correct. Employees responsible for delivering product into purchasers' custody are covered.

choices.text: Exclude the cashier because the cashier does not handle the product.
choices.why: Incorrect. Employees dealing directly with purchasers by obtaining payment are also covered.

choices.text: Train the employee directly accepting payment for these products.
choices.why: Correct. The payment-taking employee falls within the regulated seller's obligation.

choices.text: Maintain self-certification and records demonstrating covered employees' training.
choices.why: Correct. The regulation requires retention of the self-certification and training evidence.

choices.text: Substitute state pharmacist licensure for the seller's federal self-certification.
choices.why: Incorrect. State professional licensure does not replace applicable seller self-certification.

questions.topic: Purchaser cancellation of paper DEA Form 222
questions.trigger: A purchaser wishes to cancel an unshipped item on a paper DEA Form 222. What is the applicable procedure?
questions.legal_decision: Distinguish purchaser cancellation from supplier voiding and lost-form reporting.
questions.critical_exception: The unshipped item and original order documentation are the relevant facts.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the supplier initiates voiding, it notifies the purchaser in writing and records the voiding.
questions.stem: A purchaser wishes to cancel an unshipped item on a paper DEA Form 222. What is the applicable procedure?

choices.text: Erase the item on the purchaser's retained copy and notify the supplier orally.
choices.why: Incorrect. The purchaser must notify the supplier in writing; changing its own copy alone is insufficient.

choices.text: Issue a replacement Form 222 as the required method of cancellation.
choices.why: Incorrect. Written notice is the specified cancellation procedure, not necessarily a new form.

choices.text: Request DEA to invalidate the supplier's original form.
choices.why: Incorrect. Ordinary cancellation is handled directly with the supplier.

choices.text: Have the supplier return the original for the purchaser to overwrite.
choices.why: Incorrect. The supplier must document cancellation on the original form.

choices.text: Notify the supplier in writing; the supplier records cancellation on the original.
choices.why: Correct. This follows the purchaser cancellation procedure.

questions.topic: Electronic segregation and printing of prescription records
questions.trigger: A retail pharmacy is selecting one electronic prescription-record database for all schedules. It also stores images of paper prescriptions. Which Massachusetts record-system features are required?
questions.legal_decision: Require electronically separable records and readable printing, not separate machines.
questions.critical_exception: For paper records the regulation instead requires physical segregation; any additional federal record obligations still apply.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A single database that cannot separate the required categories does not meet the electronic record standard.
questions.stem: A retail pharmacy is selecting one electronic prescription-record database for all schedules. It also stores images of paper prescriptions. Which Massachusetts record-system features are required? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: A physically separate computer for each schedule category.
choices.why: Incorrect. The electronic record requirement is separability, not separate hardware.

choices.text: Electronic separation of Schedule II records from the other schedule categories.
choices.why: Correct. Schedule II records must be electronically separable.

choices.text: Electronic separation of Schedule III–V records and Schedule VI records into their required categories.
choices.why: Correct. The state rule requires electronic separability for these groups as well.

choices.text: The ability to print readable electronic prescriptions and stored prescription images.
choices.why: Correct. Both printing capabilities are expressly required.

choices.text: A second paper filing system duplicating all electronic records even when electronic requirements are met.
choices.why: Incorrect. The cited provision does not require universal duplicate paper files.

questions.topic: Accessibility of current DEA Form 222 power-of-attorney forms
questions.trigger: Where must a Massachusetts pharmacy keep applicable current DEA Form 222 power-of-attorney forms?
questions.legal_decision: Maintain current applicable POA forms readily accessible.
questions.critical_exception: This tests state accessibility, not separate federal retention requirements.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If the form is not posted but can be retrieved readily at the pharmacy, the state accessibility rule is satisfied.
questions.stem: Where must a Massachusetts pharmacy keep applicable current DEA Form 222 power-of-attorney forms?

choices.text: Posted on the wall or maintained in a readily retrievable location.
choices.why: Correct. The pharmacy-operation rule allows either method of accessibility.

choices.text: In a remote corporate archive that is unavailable to pharmacy staff.
choices.why: Incorrect. A record that is not readily retrievable does not meet the state requirement.

choices.text: At the customer entrance next to the pharmacy license.
choices.why: Incorrect. The state provision does not specify a customer-facing display location.

choices.text: Filed with each individual patient's controlled-substance prescription.
choices.why: Incorrect. The state rule does not require patient-specific filing of the authorization.

choices.text: At the wholesaler's premises instead of being retrievable by the pharmacy.
choices.why: Incorrect. Supplier custody alone does not meet the pharmacy's own accessibility duty.

questions.topic: Interstate direct delivery to qualifying LTCF
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy proposes delivering prescribed Schedule II narcotic medication to a patient admitted to a Maine long-term care facility. The prescription and applicable state and DEA registration requirements are satisfied. Which method does the specific Massachusetts LTCF delivery exception permit?
questions.legal_decision: Recognize the specific direct LTCF courier exception.
questions.critical_exception: Maine or a contiguous state, facility admission, licensure and registration are material facts.
questions.counterfactual_flip: Ordinary interstate home delivery is evaluated under separate address and carrier conditions.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy proposes delivering prescribed Schedule II narcotic medication to a patient admitted to a Maine long-term care facility. The prescription and applicable state and DEA registration requirements are satisfied. Which method does the specific Massachusetts LTCF delivery exception permit?

choices.text: Delivery to a Massachusetts retail pickup location for forwarding.
choices.why: Incorrect. The exception specifies direct delivery to the qualifying facility.

choices.text: Delivery to a facility employee's private residence for later transport.
choices.why: Incorrect. That does not meet the direct-to-facility requirement.

choices.text: Only postal delivery to the patient's former home address.
choices.why: Incorrect. Direct courier delivery to the facility is specifically permitted.

choices.text: Direct delivery to the facility by a pharmacy-employed or contracted courier.
choices.why: Correct. The statutory exception expressly authorizes this method.

choices.text: Delivery by any method once the patient signs a waiver.
choices.why: Incorrect. Consent does not replace statutory delivery conditions.

questions.topic: Abuse-deterrent interchange priority over cheaper conventional product
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts Drug Store pharmacy receives a prescription for a drug the state Drug Formulary Commission has identified as posing heightened abuse risk. No no-substitution instruction appears. A designated interchangeable abuse-deterrent alternative and a cheaper ordinary interchangeable product are available. Other requirements are met. What is the statutory selection priority?
questions.legal_decision: Apply the designated abuse-deterrent priority before ordinary price-based interchange.
questions.critical_exception: Actual state-designated interchangeability, availability and no no-substitution direction are stipulated.
questions.counterfactual_flip: If no designated interchangeable abuse-deterrent product exists, the ordinary less-expensive reasonably available interchange rule applies.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts Drug Store pharmacy receives a prescription for a drug the state Drug Formulary Commission has identified as posing heightened abuse risk. No no-substitution instruction appears. A designated interchangeable abuse-deterrent alternative and a cheaper ordinary interchangeable product are available. Other requirements are met. What is the statutory selection priority?

choices.text: Dispense the cheaper ordinary interchangeable product because price controls selection.
choices.why: Incorrect. The statute prioritizes an available designated interchangeable abuse-deterrent product.

choices.text: Dispense the designated interchangeable abuse-deterrent product.
choices.why: Correct. The statute prioritizes this product, then the eligible lower-cost alternative if none exists.

choices.text: Dispense the prescribed product because opioid interchange requires a new order.
choices.why: Incorrect. No separate prohibition or no-substitution instruction is asserted.

choices.text: Let the insurer's preference determine the statutory interchange obligation.
choices.why: Incorrect. Coverage preferences do not substitute for state product-selection requirements.

choices.text: Choose any product the manufacturer describes as abuse-deterrent.
choices.why: Incorrect. The rule concerns specifically identified interchangeable abuse-deterrent products.

questions.citation: M.G.L. c.112 §12D, definitions and substitution paragraph

questions.topic: Nonviable particle excursion versus viable remediation
questions.trigger: A sterile compounding pharmacy detects action-level nonviable particle counts in an ISO 7 buffer room. Microbiology results do not show viable action-level growth. The Board has issued no special direction. Which actions are required under the September 2026 environmental monitoring policy?
questions.legal_decision: Separate nonviable suspension from the limited viable-result pathway.
questions.critical_exception: No different Board direction is asserted.
questions.counterfactual_flip: For certain viable action-level buffer-room findings, the risk assessment and restricted BUD pathway may be available if its conditions are met.
questions.stem: A sterile compounding pharmacy detects action-level nonviable particle counts in an ISO 7 buffer room. Microbiology results do not show viable action-level growth. The Board has issued no special direction. Which actions are required under the September 2026 environmental monitoring policy? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Suspend compounding until full remediation and recertification of all ISO-classified areas.
choices.why: Correct. Nonviable action-level findings require suspension and full remediation/recertification absent different Board direction.

choices.text: Investigate the cause and implement corrective action.
choices.why: Correct. Action-level environmental findings require investigation and remediation.

choices.text: Resume with a 24-hour room-temperature BUD as soon as cleaning begins.
choices.why: Incorrect. Shortened-BUD pathways apply to specified viable action-level findings, not this nonviable excursion.

choices.text: Activate the continuity-of-care plan during suspension.
choices.why: Correct. A pharmacy suspending sterile compounding must implement the plan to meet patient needs.

choices.text: Maintain the relevant remediation records for Board inspection.
choices.why: Correct. Environmental monitoring and remediation records must be maintained and available.

critical_error_options.reason: Applies viable-result exception to nonviable excursion.

questions.topic: Institutional sterile compounding pharmacy closure exceptions
questions.trigger: A Massachusetts institutional sterile compounding pharmacy plans permanent closure. Which pair of ordinary closure obligations is specifically waived for this pharmacy type?
questions.legal_decision: Distinguish the institutional sterile compounding exception from the nonresident closure exception.
questions.critical_exception: Subsections (3) and (4) are expressly not required; other applicable closure obligations remain.
questions.counterfactual_flip: A resident sterile compounding pharmacy that is not institutional must comply with the specialty replacement-pharmacy and patient-notice rules unless another lawful exception applies.
questions.stem: A Massachusetts institutional sterile compounding pharmacy plans permanent closure. Which pair of ordinary closure obligations is specifically waived for this pharmacy type?

choices.text: Advance notice to the Board of the closure and disposition of controlled substances.
choices.why: Incorrect. The type-specific exception does not waive the general Board-notice provision.

choices.text: Patient-file transfer when legally required and postclosure return of original licenses.
choices.why: Incorrect. Those provisions are not included in the institutional exception.

choices.text: Identification of a suitable replacement pharmacy under the specialty closure rule and the general patient-notice procedures.
choices.why: Correct. The institutional sterile compounding pharmacy is exempt from the specialty replacement-pharmacy notice and patient-notice subsections.

choices.text: Postclosure return of the original licenses and attestation about controlled substances.
choices.why: Incorrect. The exemption from these postclosure duties applies to nonresident pharmacies, not to this resident institutional pharmacy.

choices.text: Advance closure notice to the Board and transfer of patient files whenever legally required.
choices.why: Incorrect. The institutional exception does not waive those general provisions.
